question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{20}$ be a random sample of size $n=20$ from a population with probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=0.04,$ calculate $P(\overset{―}{X}<0.8).$

*Hint: Assume that the sample size is sufficiently large for the central limit theorem to be applied. A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8438\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ | $\,0.8485\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8665\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8869\,$ | $\,0.8888\,$ | $\,0.8907\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =20,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{4} \\  & =0.75,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=0.04.$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(0.75,\frac{0.04}{20}) \\  & ∼N(0.75,0.002).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}<0.8).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<0.8) & =P(Z<\frac{0.8-0.75}{\sqrt{0.002}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<1.12) \\  & =Φ(1.12)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.12)=0.8686.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<0.8) & =Φ(1.12) \\  & =0.8686.\end{aligned}
$$
